title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The surrounding notes study semi-simplicial (no degeneracies), '∂-perfect' cochain objects, cosimplicial in a functor-category sense. Here C_* denotes the cosimplicial standard complex, and F_C is the functor 'tensor against C' (a coend/realization) that turns universal objects in categories like P_*, B_*, K_* into constructions on a complex C. The previous page states a transfer principle: any universal construction in these categories that uses only h-freeness/h-injectivity and ⊗-structures is reflected in a construction on a complex C in B with multiplicative structure. Example 1 there: C_*⊗C_* is a Σ-projective resolution of Z in P_{0**}, and C_* is h-injective. This gives Tot(C_*⊗C_*) → C_*, unique up to homotopy, and after applying F, a product C⊗_B C → C. That product is associative, commutative and unital only up to homotopy, which is the cochain-level 'homotopy-commutative algebra' (proto-E∞) picture.

This page, Ex. 2, proposes a better model: a de Rham complex 'with ∂-divided powers' (p.d. = puissances divisées).
- It is defined using '3 pieces' (or divided powers) as a bigraded object of some category R_*, with simplicial degree × form degree. It carries a strictly (anti)commutative bigraded algebra structure.
- In modern terms this is Sullivan's simplicial polynomial de Rham algebra ∇(p,q), i.e. A_PL, made over an arbitrary base ring (Z) by using divided-power polynomials.
- Its transform under F_C is an object of C-cdgas.
- Grothendieck notes that without the divided-power structure on R one cannot assert that the de Rham complex attached to R is strictly anticommutative and unital. More precisely, without divided powers the integral polynomial forms do not satisfy the Poincaré lemma, so the comparison fails; with them, d γ_m(t) = γ_{m-1}(t) dt and the Poincaré lemma holds over Z.
- Key acyclicity claim: in each fixed total degree, the de Rham object gives a resolution of k_* = Ψ^0_*. It is flasque, i.e. Σ-regular (the analogue of Sullivan's 'extendable' or contractible simplicial pieces), except in the maximal total degree n, where Ψ^n_* = Λ̂^n Ψ_*.
- Once it is a strict Σ-regular resolution, the universal-property argument of the previous page applies. The cdga obtained by transport through R has the same homotopy type as C's, with a comparison complex homotopy-equivalent to C. This is in fact a canonical choice, because the map DR^n_* → C_* in total degree n is unique up to homotopy.

The next page names it the 'De Rham–Sullivan complex'.

Purpose: to replace the homotopy-coherent multiplicative structure on cochains of ∂-perfect complexes by a strictly graded-commutative model valid over Z, via a divided-power Sullivan de Rham complex.
errors: Much of the page is illegible; the exact meaning of the '3 morceaux', of R_*, and of the 'exception in maximal total degree n' cannot be confirmed.

Caveat implicit but not stated: a strictly commutative model obtained this way is equivalent to the cochains only as an associative (A∞) algebra via a zig-zag, not as an E∞ algebra. Steenrod operations are not recovered from strict commutativity. Grothendieck's claim that the multiplicative structure 'coincides' must be read as 'up to homotopy as algebras', not as E∞-structures.

Without divided powers the polynomial de Rham complex over Z (or F_p) is not acyclic, so the integral comparison would fail. He flags exactly this, so the page is not in error, but the needed PD-Poincaré lemma is asserted, not checked.

ideas.what: Simplicial (here semi-simplicial/cosimplicial) polynomial de Rham forms as a strictly commutative bigraded algebra giving a commutative cochain model
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan's A_PL / simplicial de Rham–Sullivan complex ∇(p,*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Sullivan (Infinitesimal computations in topology, 1977; circulated c.1973-75); Bousfield–Gugenheim 1976

ideas.what: Using divided-power polynomial forms so that the de Rham–Sullivan complex works over Z / arbitrary base and is a resolution (Poincaré lemma)
ideas.modern_name: divided-power (PD) de Rham forms on simplices; integral commutative cochain models; crystalline Poincaré lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure — H. Cartan, 'Théories cohomologiques', Invent. Math. 35 (1976) is the likely closest reference; later Karoubi on quasi-commutative cochains

ideas.what: Canonicity of the comparison: the map DR_* → C_* is unique up to homotopy because both are acyclic (Σ-regular) resolutions of the unit, transported by the realization functor F_C
ideas.modern_name: acyclic-models / uniqueness of comparison maps between cosimplicial resolutions (Bousfield–Gugenheim, Félix–Halperin–Thomas style)

ideas.what: General transfer principle: universal multiplicative constructions in the cosimplicial model category give multiplicative structures on any complex realized from it
ideas.modern_name: operadic/E∞ transfer via cosimplicial resolutions (cf. Hinich–Schechtman, Mandell, McClure–Smith)

missed.claim: Grothendieck, c.1975-76 and independently of or concurrently with Sullivan, Cartan and Bousfield–Gugenheim, considers a divided-power de Rham–Sullivan complex in his semi-simplicial ∂-perfect framework. The aim is a strictly anticommutative integral model, and he explicitly identifies the divided-power structure as what is needed for strictness and acyclicity.
missed.quote: On ne peut affirmer encore (sans introduire la "structure p.d" sur R) que le complexe de De Rham associé à R est strictement anticommutatif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents Grothendieck's involvement with rational/integral commutative cochain models, a topic not associated with him. It links crystalline-style PD de Rham ideas with Sullivan models. Mathematically this is largely covered by later literature.

missed.claim: Several questions are left open: what structure the canonical comparison carries (E∞ vs strict), and how the divided-power structure interacts with the 'exception in top degree n'.
missed.quote: sauf en degré total maximum n (i.e. on trouve Ψ^n_* = Λ̂^n Ψ_*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The relation between PD-commutative models and E∞ cochains over Z is understood (Mandell; Steenrod-operation obstructions), so little is new.

deep.surprise_reason: It is a notable but not novel unpublished detail: Grothendieck independently working with a divided-power Sullivan de Rham complex to get strict commutative integral models in his ∂-perfect setting. The mathematics essentially matches Sullivan, Cartan and Bousfield–Gugenheim, and the page is fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: '∂-p. diff[?]' in the title is likely '∂-p.d.' (∂-puissances divisées).
'$\mathcal{R}_*$' may be $\mathcal{B}_*$ or $\mathcal{K}_*$, i.e. the categories of the previous page.
Last line: 'DR^n_* —(degré total n)→ C_* homo unique' appears to read 'homotopie unique' / 'unique à homotopie près'.
